chapter: Split, hospital and decline of tap
title: Clubs closing: the Hoofers Club, Uptown House and the Cotton Club
summary: The Hoofers Club owner gave up, new tap dances stopped, and clubs like the Uptown House and Proctor's closed while the Cotton Club held on through radio broadcasts.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: So you were saying, Chuck, that you felt at this time that tap dancing was beginning to be neglected and that the dancers were sort of going underground or into woodsheds? This was a bad -- it was beginning to be a bad time or --
No, it -- they discontinued introducing new tap dances and this new owner was going to give up the Hoofers Club. You see?
This was when, Chuck? What year?
Well -- when you got a -- when they discovered Joe DiMaggio, the Yankee Clipper. The Yankees. You understand, the days of Barney Ross and -- And --

Yeah, it was -- it was always early. In them years, you know, but -- it's something I think they had an eclipse, it was -- some kind of eclipse -- they had the eclipse -- when was that -- that's timely about it, the eclipse. In -- see they was going to Leonard Seerman used to come up there, see and then he was so -- touched by what he saw happening, you see, he introduced his play, 'New Faces' see that was trying to save these artists, you know, these
Were there other places that closed down?

Oh, yes, yes. Yes, they did. Yes, they certainly did. The Uptown House. See that went. You see? And the Proctor, and the only thing left up there then was about Lewisown Stadium, it was about the only notable -- place of -- you know pleasures, you see? They had some big hotel there called, what was that, the Reno. And it had the Rio ballroom in it, you know and then well they held out for quite sometime. They -- you know, the scarecrow got rid of the flock.
So, in other words there was a shortage of places for dancers to break in their new works and new styles of dancing?

Now, see, that was another one, see they held on for awhile, you see. But see that's because of the radio companies, you see, the broadcasts, discontinued in the Cotton Club, you see, radio shows, you see.
